comparisons.peer_summary: Micron proactively manages environmental compliance and sustainability, conforming its wafer fabrication facilities to the ISO 14001:2015 standard to ensure continuous performance improvement.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose proactive environmental management strategies, but Micron emphasizes formal ISO certification while Intel links specific emission reduction targets to executive compensation. Intel states it sets company-wide goals to reduce emissions and links a portion of executive bonuses to a specific 25,000 metric ton reduction target, citing: "In 2024, we linked a portion of the executive and employee performance bonus to our goal to reduce our 2024 Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 25,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent, compared to 2023." Micron similarly describes a proactive approach to compliance and sustainability, noting its adherence to international standards for continuous improvement, citing: "We approach environmental compliance and sustainability proactively to ensure we meet applicable government regulations regarding use of raw materials and chemicals, discharges, emissions, climate change and energy use, and waste disposal and management from our manufacturing processes." Additionally, Micron highlights its specific certification: "Our wafer fabrication facilities conform to the requirements of the ISO 14001:2015 environmental management systems standard to ensure we are continuously improving our performance."

comparisons.peer_topic: Supplier engagement for Scope 3 emissions reduction
comparisons.peer_summary: By fiscal year 2026, NVIDIA aims to engage manufacturing suppliers comprising at least 67% of its Scope 3 category 1 GHG emissions to adopt science-based targets.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose specific greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions reduction targets, but they differ in scope and mechanism. Intel sets a specific, absolute tonnage reduction goal for Scope 1 and 2 emissions linked to executive incentives, stating: "In 2024, we linked a portion of the executive and employee performance bonus to our goal to reduce our 2024 Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 25,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent, compared to 2023." In contrast, NVIDIA’s disclosed target in this disclosure focuses on Scope 3 emissions and supplier engagement rather than a direct operational reduction target linked to compensation. NVIDIA states: "By fiscal year 2026, we aim to engage manufacturing suppliers comprising at least 67% of NVIDIA's scope 3 category 1 GHG emissions with goal of effecting supplier adoption of science-based targets."

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm's 2025 goals include reducing absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 30% from a 2014 base year, reducing power consumption in flagship Snapdragon Mobile Platform products by 10% annually, and ensuring 100% of primary semiconductor manufacturing suppliers are audited every two years for conformance to the Supplier Code of Conduct.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm disclose specific, quantifiable goals for reducing Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions. Intel’s goal is defined by an absolute metric ton reduction linked to performance bonuses, stating: "In 2024, we linked a portion of the executive and employee performance bonus to our goal to reduce our 2024 Scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 25,000 metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent, compared to 2023." Qualcomm discloses a percentage-based reduction goal against a base year, stating: "Reducing our absolute Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG emissions from global operations by 30%, from a 2014 base year." While both target the same emissions scope, Intel uses a fixed tonnage target for the current year, whereas Qualcomm uses a percentage reduction target from a historical base year.
